Information since September points to a strong labor market and moderate growth, but weak business fixed investment and soft exports alongside sub-2 percent inflation and muted inflation expectations. Consistent with the interest-rate transmission mechanism documented in Romer and Romer and in Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans, the FOMC’s 25 bp cut to a 1.50–1.75 percent target range and the Desk’s T-bill purchases/repo operations should support demand by lowering financing costs and maintaining ample reserves. Still, the literature shows investment is highly sensitive to internal funds and credit conditions (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994), so uncertainty can blunt the response even when rates fall. With market- and survey-based inflation expectations low, New Keynesian inflation dynamics (Galí and Gertler 1999; Woodford 2003) imply inflation may remain below target absent sustained demand strength. Overall tone: cautiously positive given easing and strong employment, tempered by investment weakness and below-target inflation.
